title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference Architecture, Packaging, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback Library
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended reference architectures, on‑prem packaging options, day‑2 operational procedures, and standard upgrade & rollback playbooks for Private Deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and customer success teams supporting customer-managed deployments.

Scope and audience

- Scope: VPC-based private deployments (public cloud with private networking) and fully on‑prem / air‑gapped packages. Includes architecture diagrams, deployment checklists, operational runbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures.
- Audience: Eng-Private‑Deployments, customer solutions engineers, SRE, security reviewers, and customer infra teams.

Goals and guarantees

- Provide repeatable deployments that meet Redwood production SLAs when deployed to supported configurations.
- Minimize downtime for upgrades (target <5m for minor patch rollouts with canary enabled).
- Safe rollback paths for major upgrades with data migrations.

Reference architectures (high level)

1) VPC (cloud) reference architecture

- Topology: customer VPC with private subnets for inference workers, a control plane peering/VPN into Redwood control plane (optionally hosted in Partner VPC), NAT gateways for pull-only access, and an optional transit gateway for multi‑AZ routing.
- Core components:
  - Control plane connector (Redwood connector deployed in customer VPC, TLS mutual auth to Redwood control plane).
  - Inference fleet: Kubernetes or VM-based GPU nodes in private subnets (G4/ A10 / H100 families recommended depending on throughput).
  - Shared services: Logging (customer ELK/CloudWatch), metrics (Prometheus remote write), artifact storage (S3-compatible), KMS for envelope encryption.
- Networking: 25ms inter-AZ latency target, minimum 10Gbps network for GPU-to-GPU traffic for multi-GPU models.

2) On‑prem (air‑gapped) reference architecture

- Topology: customer data center with dedicated inference racks, local artifact registry (OCI), KMS/HSM with offline import keys, and an operator-managed control plane bundle.
- Core components:
  - On‑prem control plane package (bundle delivered as tar + signed manifest).
  - Artifact registry and image mirror (Harbor / Artifactory).
  - Storage: NFS or Ceph/Rook for model artifacts and checkpoints, recommended 1.5x model size headroom.
  - Monitoring: Push metrics to local Prometheus and forward critical alerts to Redwood incident bridge if allowed.

Sizing guidelines (quick reference)

| Workload type | GPU type | Min GPUs per model cluster | Min node RAM | Disk (local NVMe) | Network |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Low-concurrency inference | T4 / A10 | 1 | 64GB | 1TB | 10Gbps |
| Production medium | A10 / A100 | 2-4 | 128GB | 1-2TB | 25-40Gbps |
| High-throughput / multi-tenant | A100 / H100 | 8+ | 256GB+ | 2-4TB | 40-100Gbps |

On‑prem packaging and distribution options

Supported delivery formats:
- Helm charts + OCI images (recommended for customers with Kubernetes).
- Full air‑gapped bundle: signed tarball containing images, Helm charts, manifests, and docs.
- OVA/VM templates for customers who run on VMs.
- Appliance packaging (for long‑term on‑prem customers) — contact Solutions for customization.

Packaging checklist

1) Signed manifest (SHA256) for all artifacts.
2) Component matrix listing images, versions, and required kernels.
3) Offline install script with idempotent install steps.
4) Preflight checker binary to validate kernel, GPU drivers, available disk and network.

Pre‑deployment checklist (customer requirements library)

Network & connectivity
- Private subnets with egress rules allowing minimal outbound to Redwood artifact endpoints (if not air‑gapped).
- Port allowances (see table below).

Storage & encryption
- S3-compatible object store or NFS.
- KMS or HSM for customer‑managed keys (bring‑your‑own‑key).

Access & IAM
- Service accounts with scoped roles for deployment.
- RBAC: separate namespaces/projects per customer environment.

Minimum OS / driver requirements

| Component | Minimum version / requirement |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA driver | 535.xx (or customer-equivalent supported by runtime) |
| Docker/CRI | containerd 1.6+ / Docker 24+ |
| Kubernetes | 1.26 - 1.28 (tested) |
| Linux distro | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or RHEL 8.8+ |

Port & firewall matrix

| Destination | Protocol | Port(s) | Purpose |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Redwood control plane connector | TCP | 443 | API & control channel (mutual TLS) |
| Artifact registry (customer/Redwood) | TCP | 443 | OCI pulls/pushes |
| Prometheus remote write endpoint | TCP | 9090 | Metrics forwarding (optional) |
| Health checks / admin UI | TCP | 8443 | Local admin GUI (TLS) |

Deployment procedures (VPC/Kubernetes example)

1) Preflight (run locally at customer):
   - ./preflight-check --k8s-context=prod 
   - Validate driver: nvidia-smi, check GPU counts and memory.
2) Bootstrap RBAC & namespaces:
   - kubectl create ns redwood-inference
   - kubectl apply -f rbac/rolebinding.yaml -n redwood-inference
3) Install control connector (Helm):
   - helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
   - helm install redwood-connector redwood/connector -n redwood-inference --set controlPlane.endpoint=https://control.redwood.ai --set tls.mtls.enabled=true
4) Deploy inference runtime (canary first node):
   - helm upgrade --install runtime redwood/runtime -n redwood-inference --set replicaCount=1 --set runtime.mode=gpu
5) Smoke test endpoints (local curl + test prompts)
   - curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal.example.local/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Day‑2 operations

Monitoring and observability
- Metrics to collect (examples): inference_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, kv_cache_hit_rate, node_gpu_utilization.
- SLOs: 95th percentile token-latency < 200ms for interactive tiers; throughput SLOs agreed per-contract.
- Alert thresholds: GPU temp > 85C, GPU Util > 95% sustained for 5m, KV cache miss rate > 10% for 10m.

Scaling and autoscaling
- Horizontal: add replicas behind router for stateless variants.
- Vertical: add nodes with larger GPU type when model scaling requires more memory.
- Autoscaling policy example (keda/cluster-autoscaler): scale when queue depth > 1000 or avg latency > threshold.

Backups and artifacts
- Model artifacts: mirror to customer object store nightly.
- Config backups: etcd snapshots for k8s cluster and control connector state nightly.

Routine maintenance
- Patch windows: weekly minor patches; monthly security patch window.
- Reboots: schedule rolling reboots per AZ, avoid simultaneous restarts of all inference replicas.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Upgrade strategy taxonomy:
- Minor (patch) upgrades: rolling, node-by-node, 1‑at‑a‑time with health probes. Target downtime: 0 for stateless; <5m for minor in practice.
- Minor model config change: config rollout with canary (10% traffic), monitor metrics for 30m, then scale to 100%.
- Major upgrades (runtime or DB schema change): blue/green or shadow upgrade with explicit data migration window and customer sign‑off.

Recommended pre-upgrade validation
1) Run preflight and snapshot configs.
2) Tag current images and store manifests in artifact registry.
3) Take etcd/database snapshot and store offsite.
4) Announce maintenance window to customer and set alerting suppression.

Rolling upgrade example (Helm + k8s):
1) helm upgrade runtime redwood/runtime --set image.tag=release-2.1.0 --reuse-values -n redwood-inference --wait --timeout 15m
2) Monitor pods: kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime -n redwood-inference
3) Run end-to-end smoke test suite (see tests/e2e/smoke)--if tests fail, trigger rollback.

Rollback playbook (emergency)
- Trigger conditions: failed health checks > 3m, regression in eval prompts > configured threshold, or customer reports.
- Steps: 
  1) kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime -n redwood-inference --to-revision=<previous>
  2) Restore etcd snapshot if data migration occurred and rollback requires schema revert (coordinate with Redwood data team).
  3) Re-run smoke tests and validate metrics.
  4) Postmortem within 48 hours; update release checklist.

Blue/Green upgrade (when data migration required)
- Deploy new environment (green) with new runtime and schema migration run in read-only mode.
- Run compatibility tests against green queue.
- Switch traffic via load balancer to green during maintenance window.
- Keep blue available for 24h before decommission.

Testing and validation suite

- Smoke tests: health endpoints, a small end-to-end generation check, and resource sanity checks.
- Regression prompts: canonical 25 prompt set checked pre/post-upgrade. Threshold: no more than 2 prompts with >10% quality drop.

Operational runbooks and playbooks (links)

- Emergency GPU failover runbook: escalate to eng-serving-runtime oncall -> bring replacement node -> drain and cordon -> restore routing.
- Data‑rollback runbook: detailed schema revert steps (contact applied-ml-and-evals for eval set gating).

Ownership and escalation

- Day-to-day ownership: Eng‑Private‑Deployments team.
- On‑call escalation: Eng‑SRE -> Eng‑Serving‑Runtime -> Product on-call for customer-impacting regressions.
- SLA breaches: notify Customer Success and Account Exec within 30 minutes of detection.

Post‑incident and change governance

- Every production rollback or major upgrade must be followed by a postmortem with action items and owner assignments.
- Changes that touch control plane or customer keys require security review and approval.

Customer requirements library (summary)

- Basic: 8 CPU cores, 64GB RAM, 1 GPU (T4/A10), 1TB NVMe, Ubuntu 22.04, egress to artifact endpoints.
- Standard production: 32 CPU cores, 256GB RAM, 2x A10/A100 GPUs, 2TB NVMe, KMS integration, Prometheus + ELK.
- High compliance (regulated industries): HSM-backed KMS, air‑gapped bundle, enhanced logging retention 7+ years, SOC2-ready configs.

FAQ (short)

Q: How do I do a zero‑downtime model swap?
A: Deploy new model variant to 0.1 replica as canary behind router, validate outputs, ramp to 100% if metrics and evals pass.

Q: What if GPU drivers differ across nodes?
A: Use node pools with homogenous driver versions. Runtime will reject nodes with incompatible drivers; preflight checker flags these before install.

Docs and references

- Deployment templates: charts/README.md and terraform/modules/redwood-connector
- Runtime health metrics: eng-platform/dashboards/runtime-metrics.md
- Security requirements: security-and-compliance/audit-logging and rbac-and-auth pages

Appendix: Example terraform snippet (VPC peering)

```
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "redwood_connector" {
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc_id
  peer_vpc_id = var.redwood_control_vpc
  auto_accept = true
  tags = { Name = "redwood-control-peering" }
}
```
